objective: Give every post view its reply and repost counts, whether the viewer has reposted it, and the post it reposts, and let a signed-in user repost and un-repost a post with one call each, so the redesigned post card can show live counters and a one-click repost toggle.
acceptance_criteria: Every PostView (the feed, a thread, search results) carries reply_count (direct replies whose author is not soft-deleted), repost_count (reposts, plain and quote, whose author is not soft-deleted), and reposted_by_viewer (whether the signed-in viewer has a plain repost of it; false for an anonymous viewer).

A repost's PostView carries reposted_post: the PostView of the post it reposts, with its own counts and viewer flags, one level deep (its own reposted_post is always null); every other post has reposted_post null, and so does a repost whose original's author is soft-deleted.
Building the views for a page stays batched: the number of database queries for a page of posts is the same for 2 posts as for 20, reposts and their originals included (a test counts statements).

POST /posts/{post_id}/repost, signed in, creates the viewer's plain repost of the post (is_repost true, original_post_id set, no text, no media) through the same publish path as POST /posts, so the same domain event is published, and answers 201 with the new post; if the viewer already has a plain repost of that post it creates nothing and answers 200 with the existing one.

Reposting a plain repost reposts its original instead, so a repost never points at a plain repost; reposting a quote repost reposts the quote itself; an unknown post is a 404; an anonymous call is a 401.
Two concurrent POST /posts/{post_id}/repost calls by the same user create one repost, not two.

DELETE /posts/{post_id}/repost, signed in, removes every plain repost the viewer has of that post, together with the likes, reports and mentions that reference them, in one transaction, and answers 204; it answers 204 when there was nothing to remove; it never removes a quote repost or another user's repost.
DELETE /posts/{post_id}/repost answers 409 and removes nothing when one of those plain reposts has a reply.
After a repost or an un-repost, the original's repost_count and reposted_by_viewer in the next GET /feed, GET /feed/thread/{id} and GET /search/posts response reflect it.
POST /posts with is_repost (the /compose path) keeps working unchanged, quote reposts included.
openapi.json and schema.d.ts match the backend, and every frontend test that builds a PostView compiles and passes with the new fields.
